summary: FlameGuard is an interactive web dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA's microgravity combustion research for fire safety on the Moon, Mars and in orbit. Its main finding: crews are expected to live at 30% oxygen or more, yet none of the 208 real per-test rows we read from NASA's PSI database (BASS-II and CFI) starts above 22.2%, and PSI holds no Moon- or Mars-gravity data. FlameGuard maps this blind spot, ranks investigations by readiness for Moon-base conditions, and adds a PSI Table Checker: a browser tool that audits any PSI experimental table for missing oxygen, pressure, airflow and outcome columns and flags duplicates and impossible values. It also offers a merged starter dataset and recommended columns so future prediction models can learn from PSI. Every number links to NASA, and the site states its limits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FlameGuard turns NASA's combustion records into answers a safety planner can use. It summarizes 17 investigations and incidents (Apollo 1, Mir, Saffire, BASS-II, CFI, FLEX-2, E-FIELD, SAME and more), ranks them for Moon-base relevance, and shows real data from five PSI experimental tables.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Blind-Spot Map: a gravity-by-oxygen grid shows where NASA has evidence and where it has none. Only squares backed by a NASA source are marked "found".

2. Data Lab: real PSI tables (BASS-II 129 burns, CFI 79 droplet tests, E-FIELD 142 flames on 13 test days, SAME, FLEX-2), cross-checked against NASA's own totals.

3. PSI Table Checker: drop in any PSI table CSV. In the browser it checks whether oxygen, pressure, airflow, outcome, fuel and gravity are columns, and flags duplicate rows, gas fractions that do not sum to 1, impossible oxygen values and odd dates. On NASA's real files it found missing pressure and outcome columns, 2 impossible final-oxygen values, and 8 duplicate rows.

4. For NASA: three recommendations from the gaps, a merged 221-row dataset and a recommended-columns file to download.

5. Ask the data: answers computed live from the tables, plus Google Gemini limited to our records.

IMPACT

Prediction models need data that is complete and machine-readable. We found that oxygen, pressure and airflow often sit in report text, not in table columns. The Checker and the recommended columns give NASA a reusable way to find and fix this.

TOOLS

React, Vite, Framer Motion, Recharts, plain CSS, a Vercel serverless function, Google Gemini. Code was written with SI help (see SI section).

HONEST LIMITS

Curated sample, not the full archive. Readiness scores and recommendations are our own, not NASA ratings. The map covers PSI only; partial-gravity studies may exist elsewhere. FLEX-2 comes from test ranges, not per-run results.
